::::{#thm-smoothing-spline-large-penalty}

#### Smoothing spline with an infinite penalty is the least-squares line

Let $(x_1, y_1), \ldots, (x_n, y_n)$ be data with at least two distinct values of $x_i$.
For $\l \ge 0$, let $\est{g}_\l$ be the smoothing spline that minimizes

$$\sumin (y_i - g(x_i))^2 + \l \int g^{\prime\prime}(t)^2 \, dt.$$

As $\l \to \infty$, $\est{g}_\l$ converges to the ordinary least-squares line $g(x) = a + bx$.

::::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-smoothing-penalty.

:::
